messages:
maria: quick update — i hacked together a "migratory warmstart" prototype for shard-heavy models. goal: keep long-lived workers hot by incrementally streaming newer shard layout overlays instead of full swapouts. explores a middle ground between full hotplug and on-demand streaming. :thinking:
jon: short explainer? is this about avoiding big disk reads during peaks?
maria: exactly. idea is: primary storage keeps compact safetensors shards. worker keeps an ephemeral overlay (memory-backend) with already-decompressed/quantized segments. when we need a shard variant (eg quantized or split), we stream delta segments into the overlay and atomically switch per-layer pointers. avoids blocking all-requests while a large shard streams.
nash: +1 for per-layer atomic switch. how do you handle eviction and KV cache coherence when overlays change?
maria: eviction rules: overlay entries have lease tokens tied to request prefixes. if overlay entry evicted, we fall back to base shard with a fast on-path fallback that serves older quant/format. KV cache invalidation happens on pointer switch: we bump a small generation counter per weight-block. requests validate generation before using cached KV chunks. cheap compare-and-fence.
jon: can you paste the minimal manifest + handshake we used?
maria: sure — the worker exposes a tiny header to the loader: a manifest with segment ranges + gen. proof-of-concept: ```
manifest_v1 = {
  "model": "gpt-like-13b",
  "segments": [
    {"name": "lm_head", "offset": 1234, "len": 4321, "gen": 42, "format": "safetensors"},
    {"name": "attn_kv", "offset": 5555, "len": 9999, "gen": 42, "format": "q4_0"}
  ],
  "overlay_hint": "delta+quant",
  "sig": "sha256:abcd..."
}
```
jon: nice. how do we ensure correctness during rollover? atomic pointer swap + background checksum?
maria: rollover steps: 1) loader writes segments to ephemeral area, 2) verifies checksum, 3) publish by updating manifest gen and atomically swapping pointer table, 4) start soft-draining old caches. if checksum fails, delete ephemeral and emit telemetry.
nash: perf tradeoffs? streaming small segments causes more io ops, but parallelism helps. any numbers?
maria: on prototype we saw 20-40% lower p99 stall during model switches on our microbenchmarks compared to full hot-swap. network egress up by ~10% due to incremental transfers, but token cost stays same.
jon: what about cross-format fallback? e.g., base safetensors but overlay has gzipped quant segments. how do callers pick?
maria: routing: request policy decides prefer-quant or prefer-float. if overlay missing preferred format, we fall back to base and mark a warmup hint. also plan to add server-side scoring to proactively stream likely-needed formats (predictive warmup).
qa-bot: test plan sketch: 1) fuzz load handshake with malformed manifest (expect no crash), 2) simulate partial write + checksum fail (ensure revert), 3) concurrency test: 1000 concurrent requests during publish (measure p50/p99), 4) eviction path coverage for generation mismatches. I'll open infra PR.
deploy-bot: deploy preview created for branch migratory-warmstart, canary pool assigned (5 nodes). :shipit:
maria: next steps: formalize manifest schema (lean, minimal fields), add telemetry points for gen bumps and fallback rates, write canary load tests. thoughts?
jon: we should also define a small ABI for pointer swaps so external debuggers can introspect overlay vs base mapping.
nash: also add a metric for "overlay-coverage" (fraction of serving bytes from overlay) — helps us tune predictive warmup.
maria: agreed. i'll draft an RFC follow-up with handshake ABI + minimal schema and attach perf numbers. thanks all. :raised_hands:
